outcome: levels of lead (Pb) in breast milk
levels of cadmium (Cd) in breast milk
levels of chromium (Cr) in breast milk
levels of arsenic (As) in breast milk
non-carcinogenic health risks (Hazard Index) in infants
cohort: The study included 106 healthy breastfeeding mothers from Malaysia.
finding: A significant percentage of breast milk samples (63.2% for As, 28.3% for Cd, 97.2% for Cr, 40.6% for Pb) exceeded recommended heavy metal levels, resulting in 93.4% of infants having a Hazard Index above 1, indicating potential non-carcinogenic health risks.
mod_finding: Caesarean section deliveries were moderately correlated with increased cadmium levels in breast milk.
cross-section timing: Breast milk samples were collected 1-3 months postpartum.
